headline: Remote Expedition Planning and Registration Requirements
reservation: Registration with Parks Canada is mandatory for all visitors to ensure safety in this remote Tundra environment. There are no developed campgrounds, so backcountry permits must be secured through the Inuvik or Paulatuk offices; check official channels for current seasonal opening dates.

days.title: Canyons of the Hornaday
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Hornaday River riverbank

stops.name: Hornaday River Canyons
stops.detail: Hike along the dramatic cliffs carved by the river, offering a glimpse into the geological history of the Melville Hills.

stops.name: La Roncière Falls
stops.detail: View the powerful 23-meter drop where the river plunges into a steep-walled gorge.

days.driving: Walking only; allow 5–7 hours for canyon rim exploration
days.note: River levels can change rapidly; exercise caution near the canyon edges.

days.title: Tundra Wildlife and Bluffs

stops.name: Melville Hills
stops.detail: Trek toward the rolling uplands that serve as the primary calving grounds for the Bluenose-West caribou herd.

stops.name: Roscoe River
stops.detail: Explore the smaller river valleys that provide habitat for muskoxen and nesting raptors.

days.driving: Hiking travel; conditions vary by terrain saturation
days.note: High winds are common on the open tundra; secure all gear at camp.

days.title: Arctic Coast and Cultural Sites
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the northern park boundary

stops.name: Uyarsivik Lake
stops.detail: Visit this traditional fishing and hunting area used by the Inuvialuit for generations.

stops.name: Hornaday Delta
stops.detail: Observe the transition from riverine environment to the Arctic Ocean coastline.

days.driving: Hiking or local boat transfer; conditions vary
days.note: Insect activity is highest in July; prepare for significant mosquito presence.

intel.title: Inuvik Staging
intel.text: There are no roads to the park; long-term parking is only available in gateway hubs like Inuvik or Paulatuk. Visitors typically leave vehicles at their hotel or airport storage.

intel.title: Zero Connectivity
intel.text: Expect no cellular signal once departing Inuvik. All groups should carry a PLB or satellite phone and provide a detailed trip plan to the Parks Canada office.

intel.title: Paulatuk Supply
intel.text: The nearest fuel and grocery services are in the hamlet of Paulatuk, accessible only by air or water. Ensure all cooking fuel is purchased before flying into the backcountry.

intel.title: Caribou Migration
intel.text: The park is most active during the caribou calving season in June and July. Plan visits for late July to balance wildlife viewing with slightly lower insect levels.

intel.title: Charter Logistics
intel.text: Access is primarily via floatplane from Inuvik or Norman Wells. These flights are weather-dependent and frequently delayed by fog or high winds.

plan.arrival: Arrive in Paulatuk or Inuvik for a final gear check and briefing; verify your bush plane departure window with the pilot.
plan.vehicle: No vehicles permitted; travel is limited to hiking or paddling. Check with charter companies for canoe weight restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: The cliffs at La Roncière Falls provide dramatic shadows during the 24-hour daylight of the Arctic summer.
